blessed_one.note: FIX: Dharmamitra draft rendered this 'goddess' — བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་མ is the title 'Bhagavatī/Blessed One', not the generic word for goddess (that's ལྷ་མོ, see 'goddess' below). Flag for the second draft.

attested_check: 'TUTTĀRE' -> 'tuttare': attested: lowercase 'tuttare', no diacritic (1-5,1-10,1-20) — also resolves the TUTTĀRA/TUTTĀRE spelling inconsistency in the Dharmamitra draft, since attested is consistent

mantra.note: standardizes སྔགས (1-22, the literal word) and the 1-16 paraphrase ཡི་གེ་བཅུ་པའི་ངག ('ten-syllable speech') to the same English term, since both denote the mantra | Resolved: keeping 'mantra' (both Dharmamitra and this termbase already used it) over attested's literal 'ten letters' (1-16) — 'mantra' is immediately meaningful to a general reader, 'ten letters' is not self-explanatory out of context. Recommend Phase 2 write the fuller phrase 'the ten-syllable mantra' at 1-16 to keep the numeral detail without losing clarity.

goddess.note: kept distinct from 'the Blessed One' (བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་མ) — see note there | Reviewed: keeping 'goddess' over attested's Sanskrit 'devi' for the general grade, same reasoning as 'demons' above (devi is less familiar than karma/nirvana to a general reader; better suited to an advanced grade).

vetala.note: Dharmamitra's own choice for རོ་ལངས (vetāla, lit. 'risen corpse'); flag for reviewer — 'vetāla' or 'walking corpse' are alternatives
attested_check: 'zombie' -> 'vetāla': attested explicitly uses 'vetālas' (1-21) — Sanskrit technical term, not the English gloss 'zombie'

empowerment.note: the tantric-initiation sense (Victors 'confer empowerment') — attested confirms with 'receive abhishekas' (2-3), the Sanskrit technical term for the same rite. Kept as a separate term from 1-10's general 'power' sense.
attested_check: split off from 'power': attested 2-3 'receive abhishekas' confirms this is the technical empowerment/initiation sense, distinct from 1-10's general 'power'

demon.note: possessing/afflicting spirit (distinct from འབྱུང་པོ 'spirit', see that entry). Attested (2021 DJKR translation) uses the Sanskrit 'graha' at 1-21 but plain 'evil' at 2-5 — not fully consistent itself. Decision: keep 'demons' for the GENERAL grade — 'graha' is a real but much less common term than karma/nirvana/bodhichitta (the general register's own examples of unglossed loanwords), so it reads as general-register-appropriate to keep this in plain English. 'graha' would be the right choice if/when an ADVANCED grade is built (that register explicitly wants Sanskrit-rich vocabulary).
attested_check: 'demons' -> 'graha': attested explicitly uses 'grahas' (1-21) for གདོན — a Sanskrit technical term for a possessing/seizing spirit, not the English gloss 'demon'. NOTE: attested is not fully consistent either — it renders the same word as plain 'evil' at 2-5. Flagged below as a register trade-off, not force-applied without your sign-off.

Correction: an earlier pass in this session applied 'graha' and reported it as 'flagged, not applied' to the user — that was inconsistent. Reverted to 'demons' on review, for the reason in the note above.

yaksha.note: Not picked up by keywords.py's YAKE pass — missed entirely from the original termbase. Added from the TF-IDF pass (rank 43, count 2) after you flagged it. Dharmamitra draft spells it 'yakṣas' (with the ṣ diacritic); the attested translation spells it 'yaksas' (no diacritic), matching the same plain-spelling pattern already applied to Tara/hum/tuttare/trat/phat/ture — locked to the attested spelling for the same reason: general register, not a scholarly transliteration register. Note for the record: the ṣ character isn't in the TF-IDF script's token-character allowlist, so it split 'yakṣas' into fragments ('yak' + 'as') rather than counting it as one word — that's a real small bug in generate_en_translation_idf.py's tokenize(), worth fixing upstream if this script gets used on texts with more Sanskrit vocabulary.

might.note: Added 2026-09-24. The 'power' note already said མཐུ ('might') is kept distinct from དབང ('power'), but 1-21 had been tagged 'power'. Now locked separately.
